source.title: Rethinking Normalization and Elimination Singularity in Neural Networks
source.authors: Siyuan Qiao; Huiyu Wang; Chenxi Liu; Wei Shen; A. Yuille

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures training error and normalization effects on CIFAR and ImageNet, using different interventions from the claim versions to assess training behavior.
record.gate_note: Reports CIFAR training-error comparisons and ImageNet training-error curves for normalization variants. Also reports separate validation and downstream task metrics, which do not directly measure training classification error. Baseline results copied from prior work are identified as such.
record.test_reason: Figure 4 tests the training-speed component of V6: adding batch normalization before channel normalization, with WS held fixed, lowers ResNet-50 training error at matched epochs on ImageNet. Tables 1–2 report test errors, not evidence about near-zero training error in V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors argue that BN avoids elimination singularities, LN and GN cannot guarantee avoiding them, GN fares better than LN, and WS alleviates the problem. They propose BCN to add batch knowledge to channel normalization and report improved benchmark performance in both large-batch and micro-batch settings, with faster ImageNet training. The singularity-based explanation is the authors' interpretation of these results.
record.recipe_differences: Studies normalization interventions and their effects on error and training dynamics; it does not compare random initialization, model size, or training duration as the versions describe.
record.method_sensitivity: Normalization method, weight standardization, dataset, architecture, and batch setting are varied; reported error differs across these conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 1–2 compare CIFAR test errors across normalization methods and batch settings; Table 1 has ten entries, duplicated into twenty extracted rows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BCN+WS improves CIFAR test accuracy relative to the reported normalization baselines in large-batch and micro-batch settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 2 reports poorer accuracy and training failures after imposing heterogeneous channel statistics, and smaller channel-statistics differences with WS.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Channel-statistics heterogeneity can impair learning, while WS reduces this heterogeneity. These experiments do not measure the initialization, depth, width or learning-rate effects named in V1–V6.

record.problems: Training-error tables show nonzero errors; the paper provides no uncertainty estimates. Some baseline results are copied from prior work. Figure 4 training curves have no numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Validation error, top-1/top-5 error, mIoU, AP metrics, and statistical-difference measurements are not training classification-error results relevant to V1. No other directly relevant reported training-error rows identified beyond Tables 1–2 and Figure 4.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels, and the stated model-size and training-recipe qualifications. Tables 1–2 give test errors; Figure 4 concerns ImageNet.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-local-minimum frequencies, and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, matched plain-versus-residual comparisons, and the special-initialization exceptions.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation at initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable-depth limits.
Learning rates relative to the initial stability threshold, transient loss growth, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability training, and divergence.

Higher-learning-rate tolerance; BN versus an otherwise unnormalized network; the named MNIST, VGG and Inception settings; and Fixup comparisons. The direct speed comparison here adds BN to a network already using channel normalization and WS.

record.verdict_notes: Withdraw the record's V1 verdicts: test error cannot establish residual training error, and reduced ImageNet training error cannot establish near-zero CIFAR training error. The study is not an original source for V6. Its V6 evidence concerns training speed only.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test random or corrupted labels, random initialization as a varied condition, SGD versus Adam, model-size sweeps, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
